templates.title: First Cast Iron
templates.body_template: The cupola furnace reached 1,200 degrees at noon. When we tapped the spout, the molten stream was yellow-white and smelled of sulfur and wet slag. We poured eighteen plowshares and forty structural T-beams. For the first time in five years, the metal in our hands was not salvage cut from the convoy wrecks with a torch; it was new iron, melted from that same scrap and poured to a schedule. The children stopped playing on the slag row to watch the molds cool.

templates.title: The Tools on the Floor
templates.body_template: The Cluster school walked out of the charging floor at 08:00 and sat on the frozen quay. Fourteen children with soot on their faces refusing to lift the coal shovels. The Office said the winter would take the Cluster without the steam line. The children did not shout; they only pointed to the chalkboards where the arithmetic lesson had been erased for production quotas. We have to decide if we are building a works or a grave.

templates.title: The Falling Spear
templates.body_template: There was no siren. Just a supersonic crack that shattered every glass gauge in the turbine room, followed by the ceiling dropping two inches into the dirt. A tungsten penetrator the size of a telephone pole had come down through three layers of reinforced concrete. It had no explosive warhead — only kinetic weight dropped from eight hundred kilometers up. The Keeper called on 104.7 MHz thirty seconds later: 'Orbital track 42 confirmed. Deorbit decay is accelerating. You have four days.'

templates.title: The Signatures on Slate
templates.body_template: Today the twelve districts signed the Valley Constitution on three polished slabs of slate from the lower crypt. No titles were used. Sonya signed first, using the same carbon pencil Dr. Vel gave her ten years ago. Under Article 4, the right of any child to refuse labor in the blast furnace is made irrevocable. When the reading was done, the bell in the tower rang seven times for the living and seven times for the buried. We have survived the war.
